thread:
olivia: Heads up 1: we discovered an invoice rounding discrepancy for customer Orion on INV-8991. Usage computed $54,321.78 but invoice shows $54,322.00. The $0.22 difference got recognised in Feb as revenue. Need guidance on rounding policy for month-end.

matt: Small but recurring. Our policy per GL manual says round at invoice line level to cents and carryover rounding adjustments to month of recognition. But this is the first time it's causing a mismatch with usage reports.

jen: Is the usage source the raw metering export or an ETL-processed number? If ETL, there might be cumulative float rounding.

olivia: Metering export = 54321.778, ETL rounds to 54322.00. Invoice generator rounds line items to cents. Reconciliation script pulls ETL values.

kai: We should align: reconciliation should pull post-invoice rounded values rather than raw ETL floats. For any residual rounding diffs under $1, post a rounding adjustment to revenue AR rounding GL 4099. For larger items, do customer outreach.

matt: Proposed JE for 0.22: DR Revenue Rounding Adj 0.22, CR Accounts Receivable 0.22? Or reverse?

jen: If revenue was overstated (invoice higher than recognised usage), we should DR Revenue 0.22 and CR AR. But if invoice equals AR, then revenue needs adjustment DR Rev, CR AR. Confirmed.

olivia: I'll prepare a mass script to re-run reconciliation to use invoice-cents and flag diffs >$1. Posting JE for the 0.22 under period Feb 2026.

close-bot: Note: rounding policy update required in finance ops handbook. Assigned to @olivia.

matt: Approve posting for 0.22. For future, let's add a check in billing pipeline to output invoice-level rounded usage export.

jen: I'll file a ticket for billing infra to add that export. Ticket BI-402.

olivia: Thanks team. Will post JE and update the handbook. Thread resolved once BI-402 is live.
